name: SOS Response to DNA Damage
description: The SOS response is a global regulatory network activated by DNA damage. It involves the RecA-mediated cleavage of LexA repressor, leading to the derepression of over 40 genes involved in DNA repair, mutagenesis, and cell division control. This system demonstrates sophisticated damage sensing through ssDNA-RecA nucleoprotein filament formation and coordinated upregulation of multiple repair pathways.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on decades of biochemical and genetic research on the SOS response. The RecA-LexA mechanism is one of the most thoroughly characterized regulatory systems in molecular biology. All components and mechanisms have been validated through structural studies, genetic analysis, and biochemical reconstitution experiments.

red.description: DNA damage agents (UV, chemicals, replication stress)

orange.description: Damage detection, RecA activation, repair pathway selection

lavender.description: SOS induction requires both ssDNA AND RecA availability

notes: This flowchart represents the SOS response system with 42 unique nodes (A-BF). Contains 3 OR logic gates (ssDNA detection, LexA level check, repair completion) and 1 AND gate (RecA filament formation requires both ssDNA AND RecA availability). The system demonstrates positive feedback (RecA induces its own expression), multiple repair pathways (error-free NER and error-prone translesion synthesis), and cell cycle control (SulA-mediated division block). All mechanisms validated against structural, genetic, and biochemical studies.
